text:
Pearls are typically found in mollusks, specifically within the shells of oysters, clams, and mussels.

To enrich the artistic concept of the urban life exhibition, we can adapt elements from the hip-hop genre to describe the formation of these pearls. Just as hip-hop beats and lyrical flow echo the energetic and gritty atmosphere of city living, the creation of a pearl mirrors this urban intensity. The pearl begins as an irritant—much like the noise and chaos of the city—entering the soft tissue of the mollusk. In response, the mollusk secretes layers of nacre, a rhythmic and persistent process akin to the steady, driving beat of a hip-hop track. Over time, this layering transforms the irritant into something valuable and smooth, reflecting how the raw, unpolished energy of urban life can be refined into art. The resulting pearl, with its lustrous surface, stands as a testament to the resilience and beauty that can emerge from the relentless pace and grit of city existence.
